speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. How old are you in days, and has this vomiting been forceful or projectile?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus.

I see your history mentions a brother with pyloric stenosis, but pyloric stenosis typically presents at 3-6 weeks of age and is not associated with bilious vomiting in a newborn born six hours after delivery. Bilious vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, as it suggests an obstruction distal to the ampulla of Vater. Given the timing and severity of symptoms, we must rule out midgut volvulus immediately. I am requesting an urgent abdominal X-ray and an upper GI series to confirm the diagnosis.
